message: repositories[0] (https://packages.example.com) in composer.json sets require-published-time to false, which lets the cooldown count from the time the package author wrote into composer.json
fix: Remove require-published-time from repositories[0] in composer.json, or move the packages that need it to a repository that does not

message: repositories[1] (https://mirror.example.com) in composer.json sets filter to {"malware":false}, which skips the malware list that the repository advertises
fix: Remove filter from repositories[1] in composer.json, or move the packages that need it to a repository that does not

message: config.secure-http in composer.json is false, which allows downloads over plain HTTP: a package or its metadata can be changed on the way
fix: Remove secure-http from config in composer.json, and serve the repository that needs it over HTTPS

message: config.allow-plugins in composer.json is true, which lets every Composer plugin run its code, but installScripts in depcurfew.json denies dependency code by default
fix: List the plugins that may run in installScripts.allow in depcurfew.json (with the prefix composer:) and run depcurfew apply, which replaces true with them

message: config.policy.cooldown.block in composer.json is 0, which stops the cooldown from withholding new versions
fix: Remove block from config.policy.cooldown in composer.json, then run depcurfew apply

message: config.policy.malware.block-scope in composer.json is "update", which blocks versions flagged as malware only on update, so composer install still installs them from composer.lock
fix: Remove block-scope from config.policy.malware in composer.json
